items.title: Hono breaks when uploading "large" (>500KB) files through Multipart/Form-Data and using a middleware
Solution : Hono CSRF middleware blocking valid formData requests.
feat: warn when json validator does not find a content type in the request
items.body:
When a validator has a target 'json' it will now warn if a request is missing a `Content-Type: application/json` header.

Closes https://github.com/honojs/middleware/issues/841

Added some docs too https://github.com/honojs/website/pull/540

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [ ] Add tests
- [ ] Run tests
- [ ] `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` to format the code
- [ ] Add [TSDoc](https://tsdoc.org/)/[JSDoc](https://jsdoc.app/about-getting-started) to document the code

items.title: Feature request: support for file upload
Cannot download pdf file with hono
items.body:
hello everyone

I’m trying to return a pdf file from my hono api running on aws lambda + api gateway (deployed with serverless)

this is what I'm doing

- I call a third party provider api with returns the pdf as a `Readable`
- I consume the stream into a buffer, then send it back in the hono response
- I have configured binary media types in serverless.yml

```
apiGateway:
  binaryMediaTypes:
    - 'multipart/form-data'
    - 'application/pdf'
    - 'application/zip'
    - 'application/xml'
```

my pdf does make it back to the client but its always corrupted (the third-party api returns it just fine, so its not an error on their side) and it wont open, the response headers show `Content-Type: application/pdf` and `Content-Disposition: attachment`, but the file is unreadable

Environment details:

- hono running in aws lambda
- aws api gateteway (rest api)
- serverless framework for deployment

has anyone returned pdfs (or any other binary files) with hono + aws lambda? am I missing a step for binary encoding?

many thanks community!! 💯 🚀

items.title: request with body type multipart/form-data returning 403 error
items.body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

3.12.8

### What runtime/platform is your app running on?

Bun v1.0.25

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

I am sending a http request with content type set to multipart/form-data.
Hono is not handling the request and throwing an HTTPException error with status code of 403.

Request from frontend : 

```js
const formData = new FormData();
formData.append("id","123")
fetch(`http://localhost:5173/api/v1/admin/image`, {
    method: "PATCH",
    credentials: "include",
    mode: "cors",
    body: formData,
    headers: {
        "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data",
    },
})
```
My backend code using Hono :

```js
const app = new Hono()

app.use('*', csrf())
app.use('*', cors({ credentials: true, origin: "localhost:5173" }));
app.patch('/api/v1/admin/image', (c,next) => {
    console.log("Image update ran")
    return c.json({success:true})
})

```

items.title: Built-in CSRF helper
items.body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

It would be useful to have some sort of CSRF protection mechanism built in that users could opt in to if desired. 

OSWAP’s [cheat sheet for CSRF Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) has a few strategies that could be implemented in a helper. 

If maintainers are open to this, I would be glad to put forth a PR, as this is definitely a feature I would take advantage of.

items.title: large requests (>~100MiB) fail before bodyLimit is called
items.body:
### What version of Hono are you using?

4.3.6

### What runtime/platform is your app running on?

Bun

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

I have a use-case where a user submits a POST request to a form with around 200 MiB of image files (large images, ~10MiB each). This is how I have it set up.

1. Set up an endpoint with `bodyLimit`:
```ts
app.post(
  "/dashboard/uploads",
  bodyLimit({
    maxSize: 1024 * 1024 * 200, // 200 MiB
    onError: (c) => c.html(<Error error="Files are too big!" />),
  }),
  routePostDashboardUpload,
);

export async function routePostDashboardUpload(c: Context) {
  // there is no omitted code here,
  // it actually just returns rendered jsx
  // (crash happens before endpoint)
  return c.html(
    <Success message="Files uploaded successfully. You can check their progress in the Files tab." />,
  );
}
```

2. Call the endpoint with a large multipart body (~180MiB in this case):
```sh
curl -v \
  --location 'http://localhost:3000/dashboard/uploads' \
  --form 'files=@"/home/boris/Downloads/img/1.png"' \
  --form 'files=@"/home/boris/Downloads/img/2.png"' \
  [...more files]
```

That's the smallest reproduction I can do.

### What is the expected behavior?

It should just call the endpoint and return it's return value if the total size of the body is less than `maxSize`.

If it isn't, it should return 413. It's my understanding from looking at `hono/src/middleware/body-limit/index.ts`, that the response body in such cases should be the string `Payload Too Large`.

### What do you see instead?

However, `curl` returns the following:
```
* processing: http://localhost:3000/dashboard/uploads
*   Trying [::1]:3000...
* Connected to localhost (::1) port 3000
> POST /dashboard/uploads HTTP/1.1
> Host: localhost:3000
> User-Agent: curl/8.2.1
> Accept: */*
> Content-Length: 195543851
> Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=------------------------ae2e9d88e58090c8
> Expect: 100-continue
> 
< HTTP/1.1 100 Continue
< HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
< Connection: close
< 
* we are done reading and this is set to close, stop send
* Closing connection
```

As you can see, several things are wrong.

1. The [docs suggest](https://hono.dev/middleware/builtin/body-limit) that if a content-length header is present, it will check whether it should error based on that. 195543851 is smaller than 1024 * 1024 * 200  = 209715200, yet 413 is still returned.

2. Neither a body of `Payload Too Large` or that defined in the `onError` handler is provided, which suggests the error originates somewhere other than the `bodyLimit` middleware.

3. The endpoint is not called. I tried adding a `console.log` to verify.

### Additional information

1. I tried with different bodies and the threshold for crashing seems to be between 100 and 120 MiB, regardless of `maxSize` (set to 2GiB during testing).

2. The `bodyLimit` middleware works fine when the `maxSize` value is less than said threshold. The `onError` handler is called when appropriate.

3. Adding some console logs in `hono/src/middleware/body-limit/index.ts` also leads me to believe the error originates before that middleware is even executed.
